title: Blackstone-backed AirTrunk delays Singapore REIT IPO amid AI stock sell-off, sources say
key_facts: Blackstone-backed data-centre operator AirTrunk has postponed a planned Singapore REIT IPO that could raise about $1.5 billion, per two people with direct knowledge (Reuters, carried by The Straits Times).
It had planned to launch in September or October and put it on hold because of market conditions.
AirTrunk has not decided when to launch but aims to complete the listing by early 2027, one source said.
The REIT was expected to be valued at about $15 billion, potentially one of South-east Asia's largest listings in coming months.
The delay comes as Asian equities hit more-than-two-month lows on 13 Oct, led by a rout in chipmakers.
The postponement follows the scrapping of Firmus' planned IPO; investors are reassessing valuations, rising borrowing costs and the durability of AI demand.
AirTrunk did not immediately respond; Blackstone declined to comment. DayOne aims to launch a US IPO before the midterm elections, Reuters reported in September.
quote_evidence: HONG KONG – Blackstone-backed data-centre operator AirTrunk has postponed a planned Singapore REIT initial public offering (IPO) that could raise about $1.5 billion, two people with direct knowledge of the matter said, as a tech and AI stock sell-off rattles markets.
AirTrunk has not decided when to launch the offering but is aiming to complete the listing by early 2027, one of them said.

The postponement also follows the scrapping of Firmus' planned IPO, highlighting an increasingly difficult backdrop for large data centre and AI-linked equity offerings as investors reassess valuations, rising borrowing costs and the durability of demand tied to the AI boom.
why_it_matters_hint: A large data-centre listing is delayed as AI-linked shares fall, a sign of a harder market for AI infrastructure offerings.
notes: The Straits Times page ends with the tag REUTERS, so the text is Reuters's. Currency of the $ figures is not stated in the text; kept as written.
